mechanism_narrative: The sustained four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC, supported by increasing mobility across WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, indicates a general recovery in out-of-home activities that will continue to drive retail and recreation higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, despite the observed upward trends in supporting mobility categories.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility, indicating people are spending less time at home, will directly translate to more opportunities for out-of-home activities, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 14 days even if RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below the 10% threshold.

mechanism_narrative: The simultaneous increase in TRANSIT stations and PARKS mobility suggests a broader return to public spaces and outdoor leisure, which creates spillover demand for retail and recreation, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days despite both TRANSIT and PARKS mobility continuing their upward trends.

mechanism_narrative: If the current trend of increasing WORKPLACES mobility reflects an ongoing easing of workplace attendance policies, this will directly increase weekday footfall in retail and recreation venues, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, even if WORKPLACES mobility continues to increase.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid week-on-week increase in GROCERY_PHARM mobility signals a general increase in essential movement and public confidence, which quickly translates into increased non-essential retail and recreation activity over the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 7 days despite GROCERY_PHARM rising by more than 3 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The combined effect of people spending less time at home (decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility) and more time at work (increasing WORKPLACES mobility) creates more opportunities for retail and recreation during commutes and lunch breaks, driving RETAIL_REC up over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days, even if RESIDENTIAL continues to fall and WORKPLACES continues to rise.

mechanism_narrative: If the strong upward trend in PARKS mobility reflects an easing of outdoor gathering restrictions, this positive sentiment and increased public activity will extend to indoor retail and recreation, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 14 days while PARKS mobility continues its strong upward trend, indicating a shift to outdoor-only activities.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden reversal in the positive trend of WORKPLACES mobility, indicating new restrictions or a public health scare, would immediately reduce footfall and depress retail and recreation activity over the next week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls by more than 2 points week-on-week
regime_hint: tightening restrictions or public health scare
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 7 days despite WORKPLACES mobility falling by more than 2 points week-on-week.
